1000044.etyen:
Internationalism, based on Tswana Botswana, the Setswana name of the country. The name is formed from bo- (“country or territory noun-class prefix”) and Tswana (“Tswana”), and thus means approximately “country of the Tswana”. The further origin of Tswana is uncertain.
Parallel international adaptations include Norwegian Nynorsk Botswana, Danish Botswana, Swedish Botswana, German Botswana, Dutch Botswana and English Botswana.

1000300.etyen:
Uncertain. Probably from or remodelled after dialectal fu (“buttocks”), inherited from Old Norse fuð (“vulva, vagina”), under the influence of Middle Low German vut (“vulva”). The Old Norse and Middle Low German forms continue Proto-Germanic *fuþiz (“vagina”), possibly from Proto-Indo-European *pewt-.
A less likely proposal derives the word from Old Norse fit (“wet meadow, waterside grassland”).
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk fitte, Swedish fitta, Danish fisse, Icelandic fuð (“vulva”), Scots fud (“vulva”), German Fotze (“cunt, vulva”) and Dutch vot (“arse”).

1000556.etyen:
Internationalism, based ultimately on Arabic مُرَّاكُش (murrākuš, “Marrakesh”), the Arabic name of the city of Marrakesh, possibly from Zenaga. The country name was transmitted through European forms including Spanish Marruecos and Portuguese Marrocos. The city name came to be used for the country as a whole; the deeper etymology of the Arabic name and the immediate transmission route into Norwegian are uncertain.
Parallel international adaptations include Norwegian Nynorsk Marokko, Danish Marokko, Swedish Marocko, German Marokko, Dutch Marokko and English Morocco.

1004908.etyen:
From minister (“minister”) + møte (“meeting”), literally “minister meeting”.
The first element, minister, is borrowed from Latin minister (“servant, attendant, helper”), derived from minus (“less”). The second element, møte (“meeting”), is of Old Norse origin and is related to mot (“meeting, encounter”), from Old Norse mót (“meeting, encounter”); compare Old Norse mǿti (“meeting”) and mǿta (“to meet”).
Compare the parallel formations Norwegian Nynorsk ministermøte, Danish ministermøde and Swedish ministermöte (“ministerial meeting”).

1005164.etyen:
Compound of hvitløk (“garlic”) + smør (“butter”), literally “garlic butter”.
The hvit (“white”) element of hvitløk derives from Old Norse hvítr (“white”), from Proto-Germanic *hwītaz (“white”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ḱweyt- (“to shine”). Its løk (“onion”) element derives from Old Norse laukr (“leek, onion, garlic”), from Proto-Germanic *laukaz (“leek, onion”), of uncertain further origin. The second component, smør, derives from Old Norse smjǫr (also smør (“butter”)), from Proto-Germanic *smerwą (“butter, grease”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *smer- (“to smear, anoint”).
